page: Amazon Web Services r8i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a large 480 MB L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong capability in single-threaded tasks, with gzip compression reaching 33.41 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top tier. Single-core CPU performance and Redis SET operations perform at an average level. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4363.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 4286.46. Memory bandwidth tests also show weaker performance, with uncached large-block reads at 31.47 GB/sec and writes at 17.95 GB/sec.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong single-threaded execution, the r8i.xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute, such as caching layers, in-memory databases like Redis, and text processing pipelines.
